column8: المعاني المناسبة: ما تشير إلى وجوه المصالح وأماراتها
column9: Legally suitable meanings are those that point to the aspects of interests and their indications.

column7: Miḥakk, introduction: knowledge of a single notion is distinguished from assent to a proposition. Compare the definitional role of ḥadd in the al-Mustaṣfā prolegomenon. Text attested, but print pagination still to be controlled.
column8: فالمطلوب من المعرفة لا يقتنص إلا بالحد
column9: The knowledge sought in apprehending a thing is obtained only through definition.

column7: Miḥakk, discussion of degrees of assent: ẓann is an inclination toward affirmation compatible with entertaining its opposite, strengthened by testimony and circumstantial evidence. This provides a genuine conceptual parallel, not an identity of legal and logical situations.
column8: وهذا يسمّى ظناً وله درجات في الميل إلى الزيادة والنقصان لا تحصى
column9: This is called probable assent (ẓann); its degrees of increase and diminution cannot be numbered.

column7: Shifāʾ al-Ghalīl, discussion of the suitable meaning (al-munāsib): the distinction between acquiring a sought good and preserving it against removal supplies context for the objectives-of-law account in al-Mustaṣfā.
column8: وجميع أنواع المناسبات ترجع إلى رعاية المقاصد
column9: Every kind of legal suitability ultimately concerns the safeguarding of purposes.

column7: Miḥakk, introduction and discussion of the conditions of syllogism: al-Ghazālī expressly relates sought propositional knowledge to demonstration, distinguishing sound arrangement from the certainty of premises. The relationship is directly checked, but a quotation is deferred pending witness collation.

Miḥakk, discussion immediately following the degrees of assent: a syllogism from genuinely certain premises and correctly assembled produces necessary certainty. Useful for understanding the shift from demonstrative yaqīn to juristic ẓann in al-Mustaṣfā.
Explicit near-verbatim agreement of the exposition of simple contents and predicative relation; consult the full primary text to inspect wording and local context.
column8: فإن العلوم إدراك الذوات المفردة ... وإدراك نسبة هذه المفردات بعضها إلى البعض بالنفي والإثبات
column9: The sciences involve grasping individual subjects and apprehending their affirmative or negative relations.

column7: High-confidence verbal parallel: the same methodological pairing appears in the logical manual. Al-Mustaṣfā uses the same conception/assent architecture.
column8: فالمطلوب من المعرفة لا يقتنص إلا بالحد والمطلوب من العلم ... لا يقتنص إلا بالحجة والبرهان
column9: What must be sought in conceptual knowledge is grasped by definition, and propositional knowledge by argument and demonstration.

column7: Directly supports distinguishing the matter and form of reasoning; the legal-theory introduction should not be translated as if all formal inference were automatically certain.
column8: والخلل يدخل عليه تارة من الأقاويل التي هي مقدمات القياس ... وأخرى من كيفية الترتيب والنظم
column9: A syllogism can go wrong because of its premises or because of its arrangement and form.

column7: A genuine parallel in al-Mankhūl’s treatment of defining knowledge: the grammatical illustration is reused for the distinction between apprehending a term and assenting to a proposition.
column8: فإن المعرفة لا تتعدى إلا إلى مفعول واحد والعلم يتعدى إلى مفعولين
column9: The verb of acquaintance takes one object, whereas the verb of knowing takes two.

column7: Direct terminological parallel to the scope and sources of the discipline; compare the subsequent distinction between material studied and the final purpose of the science.
column8: وأما الأصول فمادته الكلام والفقه واللغة
column9: The material of uṣūl is theology, fiqh, and language.

column7: Shows a stricter epistemic delimitation of the term uṣūl in al-Mankhūl. This should be set against the later systematic treatment of ẓann in al-Mustaṣfā, not interpreted as an absolute rejection of juristic inference.
column8: وأخبار الآحاد ومسالك العبر والمقاييس والمستثارة بطرق الاجتهاد ليس من الأصول فإنها مظنونات بجانب أخذها مأخذ القطعيات
column9: Reports from individuals, paths of inference, analogies and conclusions obtained through ijtihād are not principles in the same strict sense, for they are probable when compared with things accepted as conclusive.

column7: Direct logical account of indication; it provides a technical comparator to the legal modes of extracting rulings from verbal evidence.
column8: القسم الأول: إن دلالة اللفظ على المعنى ينحصر في ثلاثة أوجه: وهي المطابقة والتضمن والالتزام
column9: Verbal indication of meaning falls under three aspects: correspondence, inclusion, and entailment.

column7: The qiyās of logical inference is defined as a structured argument, whereas al-Mustaṣfā I:281 defines juridical analogy through an original case, a new case and their shared ground.
column8: اعلم أن القياس عبارة عن أقاويل مخصوصة أُلفت تأليفاً مخصوصاً ونُظمت نظماً مخصوصاً بشرط مخصوص يلزم منه رأي هو مطلوب الناظر
column9: Know that syllogism consists in specified statements compounded and ordered under definite conditions, so that the investigator’s sought conclusion follows.

column7: An authorial parallel concerning the inward discipline named in al-Mustaṣfā I:7. This is a comparison of scopes and aims, not proof that fiqh and inward purification are interchangeable.
column8: وأعني بعلم المعاملة ما يطلب منه مع الكشف العمل به والمقصود من هذا الكتاب علم المعاملة فقط دون علم المكاشفة
column9: By the science of practice I mean what one seeks in order to act upon it, in addition to discerning it. The concern of this book is the science of practice, not the science of unveiling.

column7: Corroborates the division between primary and sought conception, with close verbal parallels in the opening of Miḥakk.
column8: والمعرفة قسمان: أولى وهو الذي لا يطلب بالبحث كالمفردات المدركة بالحس، ومطلوب وهو الذي يدل اسمه منه على أمر جملي غير مفصل فيطلب تفصيله
column9: Conceptual acquaintance is of two kinds: primary knowledge not sought by investigation, and that sought when its name indicates a general notion whose detail remains unarticulated.
